title: AI felt fake to me. So I made an AI terminal inspired by Doki Doki Literature Club
author: streetwearvc
selftext:
TLDR: Download it here: [gameterm.arkey.ai](https://gameterm.arkey.ai)

AI felt fake to me. Too complex. Built for people who already code. I wanted regular people to use it. So I focused really hard on the UI. I'm a big gamer, so the whole thing is built like a video game.

In Doki Doki Literature Club, the big twist is Monika. She reaches outside the game and messes with your files. GameTerm does that on purpose. The characters control your computer. They run bash. They hand coding work to Codex. They play your music.

Before anyone says Jarvis: this is not another Jarvis clone. Those projects are trash. They can't run basic terminal commands. This actually controls your computer, the way Claude Code or Codex does in a terminal.

**My Journey**

Full Disclosure: I do have technical experience. I worked as an Architect Solutions Engineer for KPMG / PwC using Python / SQL. 

GameTerm itself took about 2 months. Getting to it took longer. I built TUIs first. One of them is public: a [DeepSeek harness](https://github.com/JulianAbeleda/deepseek-harness).

Then I wanted to know what a good terminal actually is. So I [forked WezTerm](https://github.com/JulianAbeleda/gameterm) to understand it. That fork is where the concept started. I studied Kitty and Ghostty. I used and learned iTerm2 myself.

Once I understood what a good terminal is, I worked on the TUI. I really liked the original Claude Code and Codex interfaces, because the streaming looked cool. I built mine without Ratatui. It's pure crossterm in Rust.

Another big inspo was [Crush by Charm](https://charm.land).

When I got into AI, I met a lot of designers who wouldn't touch a terminal. Too complicated. But when I showed them something with a cool design like Crush, they got into it. Better reception than a plain terminal. Still intimidating. So I was determined to make something simpler.

**The characters**

The inspiration is visual novels and anime. The ones centered on AI. NieR. Serial Experiments Lain. Astro Boy. Ghost in the Shell.

* **Bridget S. Lane** is named after Lain. Greedy for information like a certain character in Re:Zero
* **Astro** comes from Astro Boy. A dog built to be humanity's best friend.
* **Leo** exists because I hate DHH and Omarchy. He's the only communist AI character.

Each one has a persona file. Beliefs. How they talk. How they answer "who are you". That is why Leo says "Doesn't matter what I am. Ask what I do."

**The art**

The art is by [u/V1hno](https://www.reddit.com/user/V1hno/). I paid him for it. His assets are the one of reasons GameTerm is not fully open source. I want to protect his work, and the work of other artists.

I followed what Obsidian did. The core is closed. Everything around it is yours to customize.

My take: AI cannot replace craftsmanship. Anything novel needs a human. Once you have a template, then it makes sense to generate. Better yet, real artists use AI better than non-artists using AI.

If this goes well, I plan to build a creator economy. Real artists sell skins for the characters. No AI art. 

This is my love letter to the history of tech. Jobs and Gates won on UI. UI is distribution.

**Under the hood**

The simple use case is a user-friendly UI. The real thing is the harness. The intelligence is fully customizable if you're into local models.

The harness is exposed. If you're into customization, you can change it. The models are swappable too. Put a model in the same folder as the rest: \~/Library/Application Support/Arkey/models/. I stuck with smaller models on install, because most people don't have the money to run Qwen3.8 27B. If you can run a better model, you can.

The stack is STT, llama-server, TTS. Multiple languages.

You run local models from files on your own disk. Or you point it at your own server. The Bridget and Leo clips ran on my RTX 5090 over Tailscale.

I'm probably switching from llama-server to tinygrad. I worked on [my fork](https://github.com/JulianAbeleda/tinygrad-arkey) until decode was close to llama.cpp on the RTX 5090. It's more of a shared kernel library. I spent most of my time on inference, because I wanted to understand how AI actually works.

**Where it is**

It's free. Fully free. I have no plans to charge for usage. Run it on local models and it costs you nothing. It's a non-technical way to use AI.

I live in NY. I've shown it to people here and got a lot of good feedback. Mac only for now.

[arkey.ai](https://arkey.ai) is a list of projects that I work on. I write a lot about AI on my research page.  

I can go deep into any part of the development. Ask if you have any questions

comments.body: I’m a little unclear on the DDLC connection?

replies.author: streetwearvc
replies.body: Have you played DDLC? The form factor for this is a visual novel. The plot twist is that Monika can control your computer. Its in Doki Doki +

replies.author: -jp-
replies.body: Yep. It’s one of my favorite VNs. Is the connection that you interface with the AI through that interface then?

replies.author: streetwearvc
replies.body:
yeah my early demos - it was rigged with Monika. I just didn't want to get sued, but you can have that as an option.
